chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik or Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man: does he inherit from his wife's house and land, from the earth (real estate), anything? Or is that like the case of the woman, so she does not inherit from that anything? He said: 'He inherits from her and she inherits from him, everything that he leaves or she leaves.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is understood to mean that if the wife has children, then she inherits from everything that the deceased left, whether it is real estate or otherwise. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.اَلتُّرْبَةِ: The earth/land, referring to real estate or immovable property in inheritance contexts
key_terms.اَلْخَبَرُ مَحْمُولٌ عَلَى: The report is understood/interpreted to mean

ai.seo_question: Does a husband inherit from his wife's real estate and land according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the reciprocal inheritance rights between spouses, with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirming that a husband inherits from his wife's real estate just as she inherits from his. The commentary by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan specifies that this mutual inheritance applies fully when the wife has children, ensuring she receives her share of all property types left by the deceased. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of equal spousal inheritance in the presence of descendants, distinguishing it from scenarios where other heirs might exclude the spouse from certain assets.
